_comment: Where each dimension letter sits on its shape image, and which
SPA.LSP answer key it feeds.
x/y are FRACTIONS of the image, so the text boxes track the image
as the palette is resized and the maps survive re-cropping.
Three things this file has to translate rather than assume:
1. The chart letters are not always the Lisp keys. The OCTAGON
and ROUND flows do line up 1:1 -- their prompts literally read
'B - overall size ACROSS', 'S1 - corner cut up the end' -- but
the RECTANGLE flow calls the same two overalls 'w and 'l.
2. SPA.LSP also uses A-D for CORNER POSITIONS (A bottom-left,
B bottom-right, C top-right, D top-left) which collides with
the chart's A/B dimension letters. Corner fields are keyed
cornera-ty / cornera-sz and listed separately so the two
senses of 'A' can never be conflated.
3. These are POOL charts. Every shape carries letters SPA does
not ask for -- H, G, F, E, M, K, L are hopper, step and depth
dimensions belonging to POOL.LSP. They are listed under
'inactive' so the form can grey them out rather than offering
a box that goes nowhere.
positions are SEEDED ESTIMATES read off the cropped images, meant
to be nudged against the real artwork. Nothing downstream depends
on them being exact.
Keys verified against the askseqb item lists in SPA.LSP.

dimensions.label: S - corner cut along the side
S1 - corner cut up the end
S2 - corner cut FACE (the tape across the cut)

round._note: a circle when the two overalls match, an ellipse when they differ
